title: What happened to the 8-bar blues and minor keys
summary: Sam asks why players no longer use 8-bar blues and minors, which express real feeling.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the blues is, and why every jazz player needs it

blocks.x: Have you listened to the top 40 jazz albums recently?

No, not recently. You see our blues, man, we don't even play our 8-bar blues no more. What happened to the 8-bar blues? What happened to it? Man, our mothers and forefathers used to sing, Bessie Smith used to sing 8 bar blues man. What happened to it? What happened to the minors? A lot of our music used to be in minors, man, because the minors give you the real feeling of expressing yourself in the minors, man. You don't express yourself in the majors, you express yourself in the minors man because you can get all - do you understand what I mean, you could get all that out of your system man, talk about it, you see. A minor is a rough key, boy. That's a rough fellow right in there, boy. You can make a tear come from a glass eye in a minor.
